issues.legal_issue: A civil court’s decision on a contested issue of its jurisdiction can operate as res judicata in a subsequent suit.
material_facts: In the first suit, the defendant appeared and objected to the civil court’s jurisdiction.
The civil court framed and decided a preliminary issue, holding that it lacked jurisdiction and directing that the plaint be returned for presentation to the proper revenue court.
The revenue court also held that it lacked jurisdiction, after which the plaintiffs filed a second suit in the civil court.
The plaintiffs did not pursue the jurisdiction question further in either proceeding.
issues.conclusion: The decision on jurisdiction in the first suit operated as res judicata in the subsequent suit, so the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under the principle of res judicata, when a defendant appears and an issue about the court’s jurisdiction is raised and decided, that decision binds the parties in a subsequent suit, even though the reasons for the decision may not. The Court distinguished Upendra Nath Bose v. Lall & Others, explaining that its statement that a court declining jurisdiction cannot bind parties by its reasons did not assist the appellants; it disapproved the contrary view in Jwala Debi v. Amir Singh. The judgment identifies the matter as one of res judicata under the Code of Civil Procedure but does not specify a statutory provision.

rule.if: later_suit_follows_prior_civil_suit and defendant_appeared_in_prior_suit and jurisdiction_issue_was_raised and jurisdiction_issue_was_decided

predicates.later_suit_follows_prior_civil_suit: A party brings a later suit after an earlier civil suit concerning the dispute.
predicates.defendant_appeared_in_prior_suit: The defendant appeared in the earlier civil suit.
predicates.jurisdiction_issue_was_raised: The issue of the earlier court’s jurisdiction was raised in that suit.
predicates.jurisdiction_issue_was_decided: The earlier court decided the issue of its jurisdiction.

issues.definition: When a later suit follows an earlier civil suit in which the defendant appeared and the jurisdiction issue was raised and decided, the earlier jurisdiction decision operates as res judicata.
